Northumberland County, Virginia Tax Sales: A Comprehensive Guide

Interested in purchasing properties through tax sales in Northumberland County, Virginia? This guide provides a clear overview of the process, including scheduling, registration, bidding, and contact information.​

Click Here to Get Dustin Hahn’s Tax Lien and Deed FREE Mini-Course

Understanding Tax Sales in Northumberland County

Tax sales occur when property owners fail to pay their real estate taxes, leading the county to auction these properties to recover the owed amounts. These sales present opportunities for investors and individuals to acquire properties, often at favorable prices.​

Scheduling and Timing

  • Auction Dates: Northumberland County does not have a fixed annual schedule for tax sales; they are organized as needed.​
  • Auction Time: Typically, auctions begin at 11:00 AM Eastern Daylight Time (EDT). However, it’s essential to verify the exact time in the official auction announcement.​

Registration Requirements

  • Mandatory Registration: Participation in the auction requires prior registration.​
  • Registration Period: Registration opens in advance of the auction and usually closes shortly before the auction commences. Specific dates and deadlines are provided in each auction’s official notice.​

Auction Venue

  • Location: Auctions are typically conducted online via platforms like HiBid. Always refer to the specific auction announcement for precise details.​

Property Redemption

  • Owner’s Right to Redeem: Property owners can redeem their property by paying all due taxes, penalties, interest, and associated costs any time before the auction. Once the sale occurs, this right is forfeited.​

Bidding Process and Terms

  • Bidding Mechanism:
    • Participants can place bids manually or set a maximum bid, allowing the system to bid incrementally on their behalf.​
    • The property is awarded to the highest bidder.​
  • Payment Obligations:
    • The highest bidder must make a deposit of 25% of the purchase price or $1,000, whichever is higher.​
    • A 10% buyer’s premium, with a minimum of $150, is added to the final bid.​
    • Full payment is typically required within a specified period after the auction concludes, as detailed in the auction terms.​
  • Property Condition: Properties are sold “as-is,” without warranties. Conduct thorough due diligence before bidding to assess the property’s condition and any potential liabilities.​

Staying Informed About Upcoming Auctions

  • Regular Updates: To stay informed about upcoming tax sales, regularly visit the TACS website and subscribe to their notifications.​
